item.title: Rethinking Entrepreneurial Finance: Multidisciplinary Perspectives in a Transforming Financial Landscape
item.content:encoded:
Enrico Battisti, University of Turin

Francesco Schiavone, University Parthenope

Digital transformation, artificial intelligence, and sustainability pressures are reshaping how entrepreneurs access capital and how value is created and financed. These changes have created new financing mechanisms while raising questions about equity and access to funding for small businesses and startups, particularly regarding collateral, legitimacy, and institutional visibility.

The special issue addresses emerging financing channels such as crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, and tokenized assets, while emphasizing that financial decisions are influenced by behavioral, social, institutional, and sustainability factors beyond technical considerations. Artificial intelligence is a key focus, as it transforms credit evaluation, investment screening, and venture creation, affecting SMEs' access to finance and requiring interdisciplinary approaches.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business and Enterprise Development. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Environmental and Social Disclosure in SMEs: Implications for Access to Capital, Investor Relations, and Financial Performance
  • Access to Capital and Financing Decisions in SMEs: Behavioral, Cognitive, and Psychological Determinants
  • Entrepreneurial Finance and Social Inclusion: Gender, Ethnicity, and Geography as Structural Barriers to Capital Access
  • Financial Reporting, Intangible Assets, and Creditworthiness in Innovative Small Businesses
  • Regulatory Frameworks and Institutional Conditions for Entrepreneurial Finance Across National Contexts
  • Alternative Financing Mechanisms: Crowdfunding, Peer-to-Peer Lending, and Tokenized Assets: Financial Performance and Social Implications
  • AI-Driven Financial Decision-Making: Credit Scoring, Risk Modeling, and Investment Screening for Small Businesses
  • The Financial Implications of AI-Powered Venture Creation: Resource Mobilization, Capital Structure, and Legitimacy in Platform-Based Startups

item.title: Sustainable Paths in Digital Supply Chains: Navigating Environmental Challenges and Technological Frontiers
item.content:encoded:
Harshad Sonar, Indian Institute of Management Sambalpur

Bishal Dey Sarkar, Indian Institute of Management Bodhgaya

Sandeep Jagtap, Lund University

Hana Trollman, University of Leicester

This special issue examines how digital technologies can be integrated with sustainability objectives in modern supply chains. Organizations are increasingly pressured to reduce environmental impacts and ensure ethical operations while managing technological disruption. The issue explores how emerging tools like artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics can enhance supply chain transparency, efficiency, emissions monitoring, and resilience while addressing climate risks and regulatory demands.

The collection seeks empirical, conceptual, and methodological contributions that bridge theory and practice in digital sustainability transitions. It recognizes that technological adoption alone is insufficient; successful transformation requires supportive leadership, training, and organizational culture change. The special issue draws on multiple theoretical perspectives to provide comprehensive understanding of how human and organizational factors influence sustainability-driven digitalization across different organizational contexts.

item.title: Corporate Transformation in a Changing Landscape: Integrating Technology, Institutions, and Governance
item.content:encoded:
Yanmin He, Otemon Gakuin University

Xikai Chen, California State University

Dongyang Zhang, Capital University of Economics and Business

This special issue addresses how digital technologies, institutional environments, and governance mechanisms interact to shape firm behavior and market evolution. Contemporary firms face complex transformations driven by digitalization and artificial intelligence alongside institutional frictions such as regulatory uncertainty and financing constraints. The special issue seeks to integrate fragmented research streams on digital transformation, corporate governance, and institutional dynamics to develop a more comprehensive understanding of firm-level adaptation in emerging markets.

The call welcomes submissions exploring how digital governance frameworks, enterprise transformation, and corporate governance mechanisms jointly influence innovation and firm competitiveness. Research may examine topics including digital transformation strategies, artificial intelligence adoption, corporate governance structures, institutional frictions affecting finance and trade, geopolitical impacts, and new measurement approaches. Submissions should make significant theoretical or empirical contributions to understanding emerging market dynamics.

item.title: Decision Support Systems for Sustainable and Resilient Transitions
item.content:encoded:
Femi Olan, University of Essex

Uchitha Jayawickrama, Loughborough University

Shaofeng Liu, University of Plymouth

This special issue seeks high-quality research on Decision Support Systems (DSS) that address sustainable and resilient transitions across organisations, societies, and supply chains. In environments characterised by technological disruption, environmental threats, and changing workforce demands, DSS models, frameworks, tools, and applications are essential for enabling evidence-based decision-making and strategic adaptation.

The call welcomes contributions exploring both theoretical foundations and practical applications of DSS across four main areas: green and sustainable transitions, digital transformation, workforce and skills transitions, and resilient supply chains. Submissions should demonstrate how DSS support organisations and societies in balancing efficiency with sustainability and resilience objectives while navigating rapid change.

Relevant submissions include conceptual models, quantitative frameworks with performance indicators, empirical case studies, interdisciplinary approaches, and critical analyses of adoption barriers and governance considerations for DSS implementation in transitions.

Appel publié par Journal of Decision Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • DSS for Green and Sustainable Transitions: DSS for integrating environmental and circular economy goals, establishing indicators and metrics for production sustainability
  • DSS for Digital Transformation: AI-powered DSS supporting digitalisation, automation, and advanced analytics in manufacturing, logistics, and workforce management
  • DSS for Workforce and Skills Transitions: DSS for workforce re-skilling, hybrid work planning, and change management
  • DSS for Resilient Supply Chains, Organisations and Societies: DSS frameworks for supply chain mapping, disruption visibility, dynamic reconfiguration, organisational learning and society regeneration
  • Conceptual models for DSS-enabled sustainability and resilience in businesses, organisations, supply chains and societies
  • Quantitative frameworks and key performance indicators (KPIs) measuring how decisions shape sustainability goals for transitions
  • Empirical studies or case-based investigations bridging theories and practice
  • Interdisciplinary methods bridging technological and organisational/societal readiness for sustainable change
  • Critical perspectives on DSS technology adoption barriers, human factors, social-economic values and governance frameworks

item.title: Transforming Retail and Consumer Marketing Strategies in the Era of the Digital Economy
item.content:encoded:
Aboobucker Ilmudeen, South Eastern University of Sri Lanka

Alaa A. Qaffas, University of Jeddah

The digital economy has fundamentally restructured retail and consumer marketing, blurring boundaries between physical and virtual commerce while intensifying competitive pressures. Consumer expectations now center on personalization, authenticity, and social responsibility, with social media and mobile platforms playing critical roles in shaping purchasing decisions. This transformation presents both opportunities for businesses to strengthen customer relationships through digital tools and challenges related to technology access, market fragmentation, and legacy system integration.

This special issue invites research examining how businesses are adapting retail and marketing strategies to succeed in digital-transformed markets. The editors seek contributions that explore the theoretical foundations, empirical evidence, and practical insights regarding digital transformation in retailing, consumer engagement, distribution systems, and business strategy to guide practitioners, policymakers, and scholars navigating contemporary market shifts.

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence is transforming small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across three interconnected dimensions: technological transformation, inclusive innovation, and territorial ecosystem development. The special issue seeks to move beyond simple technology adoption perspectives to explore how AI reconfigures organizational capabilities, entrepreneurial cognition, stakeholder relationships, and value creation mechanisms in SMEs. The call welcomes both theoretical and empirical studies that provide novel insights into how SMEs can leverage AI to achieve sustainable growth while addressing challenges related to investment capacity, skills gaps, cybersecurity, and unequal access to digital infrastructure.

item.title: Les TPE : vers de nouveaux modèles d'affaires ?
item.content:encoded:
Marion Polge, Université de Montpellier

Isabelle Calmé, Université de Tours

Colette Fourcade, Université de Montpellier

Les très petites entreprises (TPE) restent largement sous-étudiées malgré leur importance statistique et sociale. Ce numéro interroge si elles constituent des organisations singulières au-delà de simples PME réduites. Par leur légèreté structurelle, leurs interactions intenses et leur proximité territoriale, elles développent des modes d'ajustement innovants et des dynamiques entrepreneuriales spécifiques, plus sobres et résilientes que les organisations plus établies.

Depuis 2020, les mutations systémiques – crises sanitaires, défis écologiques, numérisation – transforment profondément les TPE. Le numéro explore comment elles réinventent la performance au-delà de la croissance, adoptant des approches multiformes axées sur l'équilibre, la durabilité et l'impact local. Les nouvelles technologies créent tant des opportunités que des vulnérabilités pour ces organisations.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Trajectoires stratégiques atypiques et diversification des profils de dirigeants de TPE : profils, motivations, rapport au travail et au risque, bifurcations de parcours
  • Redéfinition de la performance dans les TPE : indicateurs alternatifs, refus de la croissance, équilibre de vie, ancrage territorial, relations au vivant
  • TPE, écologie et raréfaction des ressources : modèles économiques frugaux, économie circulaire, décroissance choisie, entreprise régénérative, impact écologique
  • TPE et technologies : appropriation, marginalisation ou résistance face à la numérisation, à l'intelligence artificielle, à l'ubérisation ou à la plate-forme-économie
  • Formes alternatives d'organisation et d'innovation : bricolage, mutualisation, coopération, hybridation des statuts, pratiques informelles ou hybrides
  • Rôle des TPE dans les transitions sociales et territoriales : résilience locale, dynamiques d'inclusion, réponses aux crises systémiques, justice économique
  • Méthodologies et épistémologies de recherche adaptées aux TPE : recherches partenariales, approches critiques, récits de vie, ethnographie entrepreneuriale

item.title: Digital and AI Transformation in Insurance
item.content:encoded:
Anja Grujovic-Vischer, The Geneva Association

Ruo Jia, Peking University

Zhiyu Quan, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

Digital technologies, artificial intelligence, data science, InsurTechs, and automation are reshaping how risks are identified, priced, mitigated, transferred, managed, and regulated. These developments raise important questions not only for re/insurers and regulators, but also for the wider research community.

This special issue welcomes high-quality empirical, experimental, policy-oriented, and practice-based contributions that deepen our understanding of digital and AI transformation in insurance and related risk-transfer markets. We particularly encourage submissions that speak to broad academic debates while offering clear implications for insurance markets, insurers, consumers, regulators, and society.

Appel publié par The Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance Issues and Practice. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Artificial intelligence applications in insurance
  • Data science in risk identification and pricing
  • InsurTechs and automation in insurance
  • Risk mitigation and transfer in digital contexts
  • Insurance regulation in the digital age
  • Consumer implications of digital transformation
  • Societal impacts of AI in insurance

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Building Digital Capabilities for Improved ESG Performance of Entrepreneurial Firms: Strategies for Tackling Challenges and Capitalizing on Opportunities
item.content:encoded:
Stefano Bresciani, University of Torino

Jawad Abbas, James Cook University

Fauzia Jabeen, Abu Dhabi University

Technological advancements require entrepreneurial firms to strategically develop digital capabilities to enhance their competitiveness, innovation capacity, and sustainable performance. This collection seeks to explore how such firms build digital capabilities to improve their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance while addressing challenges in integrating digital solutions for sustainability.

The collection recognizes that entrepreneurial ventures, characterized by innovation and agility, play a critical role in advancing digital-driven sustainable business practices. Improved ESG performance is essential for managing environmental and social risks, enhancing corporate reputation, and meeting stakeholder expectations regarding ethical and responsible business conduct. The collection welcomes experimental, conceptual, theoretical, and empirical studies that examine the intersection of digital capabilities and ESG performance in entrepreneurial firms, illuminate obstacles, and propose practical solutions.

Appel publié par International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How do entrepreneurial ventures define and measure ESG performance in the digital era? What critical digital capabilities contribute to their improved ESG performance?
  • What challenges do entrepreneurial firms face in integrating digital solutions to enhance environmental sustainability? What could be the best practices for tackling those challenges?
  • What are the possible learning mechanisms and knowledge-sharing processes within entrepreneurial ecosystems that could foster development of digital capabilities for ESG goals?
  • What roles do leadership and organizational culture play in fostering digital capabilities for superior ESG performance in entrepreneurial firms?
  • How can entrepreneurial firms effectively utilize digital technologies to measure and improve their environmental performance within ESG frameworks?
  • How can digital capabilities be harnessed to address diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) challenges in entrepreneurial firms, contributing to improved social sustainability?
  • How do digitalization efforts impact the governance structures of entrepreneurial firms in the context of sustainability? What actions could be taken to improve it?
  • To what extent do regulatory frameworks influence the adoption of digital strategies for ESG compliance in entrepreneurial settings?
  • How do digital technologies facilitate transparency and accountability in ESG reporting for entrepreneurial firms?
  • How can entrepreneurial firms balance profitability goals with sustainable practices through digital transformations? Under this scenario, which opportunities and challenges could arise?
  • What lessons can we learn from recent, real-world cases that showcase the impact of digital capabilities on ESG performance in different industries, particularly entrepreneurial firms, and how can new guidelines lead toward improved ESG performance?

item.title: From Adoption to Impact: Post-Adoption, Value Realization, and Societal Transformation of ICT and AI
item.content:encoded:
Jyoti Choudrie, University of Hertfordshire

Sherah Kurnia, The University of Melbourne

Gabrielle Peko, University of Auckland

David Sundaram, University of Auckland

This special issue addresses the critical gap between technology adoption and actual value realization, focusing on how organizations and societies integrate, adapt, and leverage ICTs and AI beyond their initial implementation. While existing research emphasizes adoption decisions, there remains limited understanding of post-adoption dynamics, continued use, and the translation of technological investments into tangible organizational and societal benefits.

The issue welcomes research exploring post-adoption phenomena across individual, organizational, and societal levels, including technology assimilation, value creation, and transformation. It also addresses significant risks and ethical concerns arising from ICT and AI deployment, such as algorithmic bias, privacy threats, digital inequality, and unintended consequences that require scholarly attention.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Post-adoption behaviors: continued use, discontinuance, and switching

  • Changes to work practices, organizational structures, and decision-making
  • ICT-enabled institutional and governance transformation
  • Digital platforms, ecosystems, and network effects
  • Public sector and societal impacts of sustained technology use
  • Success and failure of digital transformation initiatives
  • Algorithmic bias, transparency, and accountability
  • Privacy, cybersecurity, and data governance challenges
  • Overuse, misuse, and unintended consequences of ICTs and AI
  • Environmental and societal externalities of digital technologies
  • Regulation and governance of AI and digital technologies
  • Organizational strategies for effective post-adoption management
  • Public policy for sustainable and ethical technology use

item.title: Responsible and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Tourism and Hospitality
item.content:encoded:
Brian King, Texas A&M University

Kyoung Jun Lee, Kyung Hee University

Danae Manika, Brunel University of London

Babak Taheri, Texas A&M University

This special issue seeks to advance understanding of how artificial intelligence can be designed and deployed responsibly and trustworthily within tourism and hospitality sectors. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in service delivery, marketing, operations, and guest experiences, the sector faces both opportunities for innovation and significant ethical challenges regarding fairness, accountability, transparency, and consumer trust.

The special issue invites interdisciplinary research examining the technical, managerial, legal, and societal dimensions of responsible AI adoption. Submissions should explore the design, governance, and impacts of AI-enabled platforms and systems, addressing topics such as algorithmic bias, consumer trust, sustainable AI applications, ethical frameworks, digital transformation, and labor implications within tourism and hospitality contexts.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Generative AI in marketing: pursuing responsibility in branding, engagement, and consumer journeys

  • AI, sustainability, and CSR: supporting or hindering responsible and sustainable practices in tourism and hospitality

  • Social and labor impacts: the effects of adopting AI on employment, equity, and workforce well-being
  • Frugal AI and digital twins: cost-effective and resource-conscious applications for operations and guest experiences
  • Algorithmic transparency and rights: making AI decisions understandable and offering recourse for affected consumers
  • Dark side of AI: risks of manipulation, surveillance, over-automation, and addictive design
  • Corporate digital responsibility (CDR) in the age of AI within tourism and hospitality
  • AI on digital platforms: exploring recommender systems, marketplaces, and platform governance

item.title: Digital Transformation and Service
item.content:encoded:
Christian Bartelheimer, University of Göttingen

Daniel Beverungen, Paderborn University

Sara Hofmann, University of Agder

Lysanne Lessard, University of Ottawa

This topical collection examines how digital transformation and service shape contemporary information systems, particularly focusing on value creation across organizational boundaries through digital technologies, platforms, and ecosystems. The collection seeks theoretically grounded research that goes beyond broad claims about digital transformation to instead examine how IT artifacts are designed and applied to enable value co-creation in service contexts.

The collection prioritizes submissions that explicitly analyze IT artifacts rather than treating them as black boxes, showing how these artifacts shape and are shaped by organizational digital transformation. Research should be grounded in IS literature and address relevant gaps for both theory and practice, with particular interest in inter-organizational and platform-based service scenarios relevant to Electronic Markets.

item.title: Unpacking Digitalization: Antecedents, Strategies, and Performance Implications
item.content:encoded:
Jasmina Berbegal-Mirabent, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya

Angelo Cavallo, Politecnico di Milano

Antje Fiedler, University of Auckland

Esteban Lafuente, Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica

Digital technologies are fundamentally reshaping how both private and public organizations—including universities, hospitals, and local administrations—conceive strategy, innovate, and compete. However, scholarly understanding remains fragmented regarding how digitalization operates across different functional areas and organizational levels, and literature has not fully clarified the mechanisms through which technological adoption generates performance gains or the conditions under which it falters.

Appel publié par Review of Managerial Science. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Antecedents of digital technologies adoption: Strategic approaches including organizational, technological, institutional, and market-related factors influencing SMEs' digitalization strategies
  • Differences in digitalization strategies between industries or economic contexts
  • Strategic choices and prerequisites supporting digitally-induced organizational actions
  • Socio-technical system readiness factors including technical infrastructure, organizational culture, workforce capabilities, and data governance maturity
  • Ecosystem characteristics and their role in shaping digitally enabled interactions
  • Human-technology interaction and integration of digital technologies into firm operations

item.title: Beyond AI: HRM and the Work of the Future
item.content:encoded:

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence and related technologies are transforming human resource management practices and the future of work. Building on two decades of e-HRM research, the collection seeks to understand how AI differs from previous technological advances, what new capabilities it offers for HRM, and what challenges or limitations need to be addressed. The issue welcomes both papers presented at the 10th e-HRM Conference in Muenster (June 2026) and submissions from researchers unable to attend.

The collection addresses critical questions about which HRM processes should be automated versus augmented through AI, how to mitigate concerns about bias and inequality, and how to maintain human agency and trust in AI-enabled systems. It emphasizes the role of academic research in providing evidence-based guidance on responsible AI implementation in organizations, ensuring benefits for all stakeholders including employees, managers, and organizations.

item.title: Crossing Methodological Borders: Mixed-/Multi-Methods in Contemporary Industrial and Information Systems management
item.content:encoded:
As digital technologies increasingly transform industrial operations, integrating industrial management with information systems (IS/IT) research has become essential. Key domains such as supply chain resilience, digital innovation, and data-driven decision-making require methodological approaches that can address both technical complexity and organizational dynamics.

However, many existing studies still rely predominantly on either primary or secondary data, with relatively few exploring the benefits of strategically combining the two. Integrating primary data (e.g., surveys, interviews, experiments) with secondary data (e.g., ERP logs, platform analytics, archival datasets) enables deeper theory development by revealing both behavioral patterns and underlying mechanisms.

item.title: Multinational enterprises, sustainability and innovation in the digital age: Global, regional and local perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Achieving net-zero targets poses significant challenges for economies, governments, and societies worldwide. Multinational enterprises (MNEs) are central actors in this transition, both as developers and adopters of renewable energy and low-carbon technologies. As primary boundary spanners, they manage global value chains and partnerships across diverse institutional contexts and consumer markets. MNEs increasingly navigate a complex landscape of incentives, sanctions, and regulatory barriers that vary by sector, technology platform, country, and region. Politically motivated disruptions—including shifting tariff and non-tariff barriers and uneven low-carbon policies—compound these challenges, placing premium value on managerial capabilities.

Two emerging developments motivate this Special Issue. First, digital technologies offer new potential to enhance firm-level capabilities for coordinating and adapting cross-border networks, while reshaping competitive dynamics between incumbents, startups, and scale-ups. Second, China's ascendancy as both innovator and regulator—particularly in new energy technologies—and its growing geopolitical influence demand renewed scholarly attention.

The concept of luxury is undergoing significant changes in the digital age, merging traditional ideas of exclusivity and craftsmanship with innovative digital experiences. Technology increasingly influences our daily lives as luxury brands increasingly apply digital tools to enhance the customer experience, reshaping the luxury markets and fundamentally altering how luxury is perceived, experienced, and consumed. Additionally, changing societal norms and consumer expectations require luxury brands to engage in new ways, such as through brand activism. This transformation impacts how luxury brands connect with consumers and deliver value.

Virtual contact points are increasingly replacing or supplementing human interactions, providing personalized and seamless experiences. Consumers can now display their luxury consumption on social media and explore and interact with luxury products through immersive virtual experiences, such as digital flagship stores, which blur the lines between physical and digital realms. item.title: Thriving Through Transformation: Employee Experience, Resilience, and Human Sustainability in Changing Workplaces
item.content:encoded:
Contemporary organisations are increasingly operating under conditions of continuous transformation shaped by digital disruption, artificial intelligence (AI), hybrid work arrangements, sustainability transitions, and persistent workforce uncertainty. Unlike earlier planned and episodic approaches to organisational change, transformation today is experienced as ongoing, psychologically demanding, and open-ended, placing sustained pressure on employees, managers, and teams to adapt and remain engaged under conditions of deep uncertainty. At the same time, organisations are expected not only to transform effectively, but also to sustain employee wellbeing, resilience, inclusion, meaningful work, and healthy organisational functioning throughout prolonged change processes.

Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) encompasses essential systems and services that are vital for societal stability, economic security, and national safety. The increasing digitalization of these infrastructures has introduced unprecedented efficiencies that have transformed economies, enabling faster service delivery, improved public safety, reduced corruption, and enhanced crisis response through data sharing and analytics.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) supports digital public infrastructure (DPI) as a driver for financial inclusion, social protection, and governance reforms. Digital advancements have also driven sustainability, with smart grids, environmental monitoring, and optimized resource management with potential for reducing carbon footprints and increasing resilience.

Potential topics

  • Emerging Technologies and Digital Transformation: Innovative technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Digital Twins, Blockchain and IoT are transforming CNI, enabling predictive analytics, smart grids, and cyber-physical security enhancements.
  • Cybersecurity, Resilience, and Risk Management: Cyber threats such as ransomware, insider attacks, and cyber-physical vulnerabilities continue to grow. Risk assessment frameworks and mitigation strategies are essential.
  • Governance, Policy, and Public-Private Partnerships: CNI governance requires polycentric collaborative efforts between government agencies, private sector entities, and international stakeholders.
